def find_inverted(s, minstem=8, minloop=0, maxloop=20):
    hits=[]
    L=minstem
    while L<=15:
        for i in range(0, len(s)-2*L-maxloop):
            stem=s[i:i+L]
            for loop in range(minloop, maxloop+1):
                j=i+L+loop
                if j+L>len(s): break
                if s[j:j+L]==rc(stem):
                    hits.append((L,loop,i,j+L,stem))
        L+=1
    return hits

## Report: `region.fasta` (sequence `region_011`)

**Sequence basics**
- 3,000 bp, no ambiguous bases. Composition: A 25.3%, C 24.5%, G 23.4%, T 26.9% → **GC 47.9%**, typical of a bacterial-style genome.
- No tandem/direct repeats ≥12 bp, no inverted repeats or hairpins ≥8-bp stem, no low-complexity runs.

**Main finding: one unambiguous protein-coding gene on the + strand**

| Feature | Coordinates (1-based, inclusive) |
|---|---|
| CDS (ATG…last sense codon) | **1161–2174 (+ strand)** |
| Start codon (ATG) | 1161–1163 |
| Stop codon (TAA) | 2175–2177 |
| In-frame stop immediately upstream | TGA at 1149–1151 |

- 1,014 bp = **338 codons**, and the translated 338-aa protein contains **no internal stop codons**.
- It has a strong coding signature: **GC at 3rd codon positions = 71%**, versus ~45% for the whole 3 kb — a +24-point codon-position bias. A 338-codon ORF arising by chance in a 3-kb sequence is essentially impossible (p ≈ 10⁻⁴ by composition-matched shuffling), so this is a genuine CDS.
- The gene is compositionally distinct from its surroundings: ORF GC = 54.8% vs **43.7%** in 1–1159 and **45.2%** in 2177–3000. A locally GC-rich gene embedded in a lower-GC background is the classic signature of a recently acquired (horizontally transferred) gene, though it can also just reflect strong codon bias.

**The encoded protein (~39.3 kDa)**
- Soluble, globular: no hydrophobic window above 1.1 (Kyte–Doolittle, 19-aa window) → **no signal peptide and no transmembrane segments**.
- Highly basic overall (K+R+H = 61 vs D+E = 37; net charge ≈ +24), Arg-rich (27 Arg), with an unusual scarcity of cysteine (**1 Cys**) and few aromatics (7 Trp, 7 Tyr). No recognizable short motifs (no P-loop/Walker A, no HTH, no Zn-finger). Function cannot be assigned from the sequence alone; this is a **protein of unknown function**.

**Secondary observation (lower confidence): long ORFs on the − strand**

The − strand carries four ORFs >100 aa, which is more than expected by chance (p ≈ 10⁻⁴ by shuffling):

- 2694–2996 (101 aa), stop 2692–2694
- 2218–2694 (159 aa), stop 2216–2218
- 1476–1829 (118 aa), stop 1474–1476
- 240–953 (**238 aa**), stop 238–240

Two of these (2694–2996 and 2218–2694) are arranged head-to-tail with a canonical overlapping **ATG/TGA ("ATGA") stop–start junction** at ~2691–2694 and a plausible ribosome-binding site (`AGGA`) ~12 nt upstream of the 2218 start — the hallmark of translationally coupled genes in an operon. However, **none of these ORFs shows any codon-position GC bias** (GC3 ranges 37–58%, i.e. equal to or below GC1/GC2), unlike the + strand gene. So while one or two may be real, they are more plausibly chance ORFs (favoured here because AT-rich sequence in the flanks and the GC-rich central block both distort stop-codon frequencies). I would not call them genes on this evidence alone.

**Bottom line**
The only feature that clearly stands out is a single strong protein-coding gene at **1161–2174 (+ strand)** encoding a 338-aa, ~39-kDa soluble, Arg-rich protein of unknown function, set in an otherwise gene-poor, repeat-free, 48%-GC background. No regulatory hairpins, repeats, or other notable motifs were detected.
